bmt-2012-team-01.prompt: Let $S$ be the set of all rational numbers $x\in[0,1]$ with repeating base $6$ expansion $x=0.\overline{a_1a_2\cdots a_k}=0.a_1a_2\cdots a_ka_1a_2\cdots a_k\cdots$ for some finite sequence $\{a_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of distinct nonnegative integers less than $6$. What is the sum of all numbers that can be written in this form? (Put your answer in base $10$.)

bmt-2012-team-02.prompt: Evaluate $$\prod_{k=1}^{254}\log_{k+1}\!\big((k+2)^{u_k}\big),\qquad\text{where } u_k=\begin{cases}-k & k\text{ odd}\\ \dfrac{1}{k-1} & k\text{ even.}\end{cases}$$

bmt-2012-team-03.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with side lengths $AB=2011$, $BC=2012$, $AC=2013$. Create squares $S_1=ABB'A''$, $S_2=ACC''A'$ and $S_3=CBB''C'$ on the sides $AB$, $AC$, $BC$ respectively, each lying on the opposite side of its side from the triangle. Let square $S_4$ have side length $A''A'$, square $S_5$ have side length $C''C'$, and square $S_6$ have side length $B''B'$. Let $A(S_i)$ be the area of square $S_i$. Compute $$\frac{A(S_4)+A(S_5)+A(S_6)}{A(S_1)+A(S_2)+A(S_3)}.$$

bmt-2012-team-04.prompt: There are $12$ people labeled $1,\dots,12$ working together on $12$ missions, with people $1,\dots,i$ working on the $i$th mission. There is exactly one spy among them. If the spy is not working on a mission, it will be a huge success, but if the spy is working on the mission, it will fail with probability $1/2$. Given that the first $11$ missions succeed and the $12$th mission fails, what is the probability that person $12$ is the spy?

bmt-2012-team-05.prompt: Let $p>1$ be relatively prime to $10$. Let $n$ be a positive integer and $d$ its last digit. Define $f(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{10}\right\rfloor+d\cdot m$. We call $m$ a *divisibility multiplier* for $p$ if $f(n)$ is divisible by $p$ if and only if $n$ is divisible by $p$. Find a divisibility multiplier for $2013$.

bmt-2012-team-06.prompt: A circle with diameter $\overline{AB}$ is drawn, and the point $P$ is chosen on segment $\overline{AB}$ so that $\frac{AP}{AB}=\frac1{42}$. Two new circles $a$ and $b$ are drawn with diameters $\overline{AP}$ and $\overline{PB}$ respectively. The perpendicular line to $\overline{AB}$ passing through $P$ intersects the (original) circle twice at points $S$ and $T$. Two more circles $s$ and $t$ are drawn with diameters $\overline{SP}$ and $\overline{ST}$ respectively. For any circle $\omega$ let $A(\omega)$ denote its area. What is $\dfrac{A(s)+A(t)}{A(a)+A(b)}$?
bmt-2012-team-06.reviewNote: Official solution gives 1763/841 (it takes the diameter of s to be sqrt(1-p^2) rather than sqrt(p(1-p)), which contradicts SP^2=AP*PB). Stored answer 205/1682 is our own computation; please check.

bmt-2012-team-07.prompt: Suppose Bob begins walking at a constant speed from point N to point S along the path indicated in the figure (segments of lengths $1,\tfrac12,\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\dots$, turning at right angles). After Bob has walked a distance of $x$, Alice begins walking at point N, heading towards point S along the same path. Alice walks $1.28$ times as fast as Bob when they are on the same line segment and $1.06$ times as fast as Bob otherwise. For what value of $x$ do Alice and Bob meet at point S?

bmt-2012-team-08.prompt: Let $\varphi$ be the Euler totient function and let $\varphi^k(n)$ be $\varphi$ composed with itself $k$ times. Define $\theta(n)=\min\{k\in\mathbb N\mid\varphi^k(n)=1\}$. For example $\varphi(13)=12$, $\varphi^2(13)=4$, $\varphi^3(13)=2$, $\varphi^4(13)=1$, so $\theta(13)=4$. Let $f(r)=\theta(13^r)$. Determine $f(2012)$.

bmt-2012-team-09.prompt:
A permutation of a set is a bijection from the set to itself. For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ written as the ordered list $(\sigma(1),\dots,\sigma(n))$, let
$$\theta_k(m)=\begin{cases}m+1&m<k\\1&m=k\\m&m>k.\end{cases}$$
Call a finite sequence $\{a_i\}_{i=1}^j$ a *disentanglement* of $\sigma$ if $\theta_{a_j}\circ\cdots\circ\theta_{a_1}\circ\sigma$ is the identity permutation. For example, when $\sigma=(3,2,1)$, then $\{2,3\}$ is a disentanglement of $\sigma$. Let $f(\sigma)$ denote the minimum length of a disentanglement of $\sigma$. Let $g(n)$ be the expected value of $f(\sigma)$ for a random permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$. What is $g(6)$?
bmt-2012-team-09.reviewNote: Official answer is 197/60: its solution computes E[L] as sum of j/j! (163/60) instead of sum of P(L>=j)=1/j! (1237/720). Stored 3083/720 confirmed by exhaustive BFS over all 720 permutations; please check.

bmt-2012-team-10.prompt: Suppose that $728$ coins are set on a table, all facing heads up at first. For each iteration, we randomly choose $314$ coins and flip them (from heads to tails or vice versa). Let $\frac ab$ be the expected number of heads after we finish $4001$ iterations, where $a$ and $b$ are relatively prime. Find $(a+b)\bmod 10000$.
bmt-2012-team-10.reviewNote: Official answer is 8753; its closed form for a/b is garbled (uses 1004001 for 100^4001 etc.). Our exact big-integer computation of the reduced fraction gives a+b = 6745 (mod 10000); please check.
